Linde stock raises 2026 outlook after record third quarter
sum: Linde reported record third-quarter sales and adjusted earnings on Thursday, October 29, while raising its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings outlook. The industrial gases company said demand in electronics, chemicals and energy, and manufacturing supported the quarter. Its release was carried by Morningstar via Business Wire.

Sales reached 9.404 billion US dollars, an increase of 9 percent from the prior-year quarter. Underlying sales rose 5 percent, with price attainment contributing 3 percent and volumes 2 percent. Adjusted operating profit increased 8 percent to 2.763 billion US dollars, producing an adjusted operating margin of 29.4 percent.

Reported diluted EPS fell 11 percent to 3.66 US dollars because of purchase-accounting effects and cost-reduction and other charges. On an adjusted basis, EPS rose 9 percent to 4.59 US dollars, while adjusted net income increased 7 percent to 2.122 billion US dollars. Operating cash flow gained 8 percent to 3.169 billion US dollars, and free cash flow totaled 1.777 billion US dollars after capital spending.

Management raised the full-year adjusted EPS range to 17.82 to 17.92 US dollars from 17.70 to 17.90 US dollars, assuming a 2 percent favorable currency effect. The company expects fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of 4.40 to 4.50 US dollars, representing growth of 5 to 7 percent from the year-earlier quarter. Planned 2026 capital spending remains between 5.5 billion and 6.0 billion US dollars.

Electronics sales grew 15 percent year over year, according to Reuters, published by Fidelity. The report linked the strongest end-market performance to demand for gases used in semiconductor manufacturing as producers expand capacity for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing chips.

Chief Executive Officer Sanjiv Lamba said proposal activity remained robust, particularly in electronics, and that Linde expected continued backlog growth. The company reported a project backlog of 11 billion US dollars and said it was focusing on productivity, operational execution, and disciplined capital deployment.

sum: The company is a leading industrial gases company engaged in manufacturing and supplying atmospheric gases, process gases and speciality gases. Its products and services cater to industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, metals, chemicals, food processing and energy. The company also provides engineering solutions and equipment for gas production, storage and distribution.

The Nifty 50 is trading at 23,930.55, up by 0.55%, while the Sensex gained to 77,296.33, up by 0.49% on Wednesday. The shares of Linde India are currently trading at Rs. 6,127.00, up by 6.67%. The company has a market capitalisation of Rs. 52,253.64 crore. The stock’s 52 week high is Rs. 8,049.00 and its 52 week low is Rs. 5,544.00. In the past 6 months, the stock has delivered a return of -17.61%.

Linde India announced its consolidated financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 12.3% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs. 723 crore from Rs. 644 crore in Q2 FY26.

However, the company's operating profitability declined during the quarter. EBITDA fell 18% year-on-year to Rs. 232 crore compared with Rs. 282 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. EBITDA margin also contracted sharply to 32% from 43.8%.

The company's consolidated net profit declined 30.5% to Rs. 119 crore from Rs. 171 crore in Q2 FY26. The fall in profitability despite higher revenue highlights the impact of rising operating expenses on the company's financial performance.

Looking at the quarterly results of Linde India Limited, consolidated revenue from operations increased by 12.3% year-on-year to Rs. 723.2 crore in Q2 FY27 compared with Rs. 644.2 crore in Q2 FY26. On a sequential basis, revenue increased by 4.2% from Rs. 694.4 crore in Q1 FY27.

The company's consolidated EBITDA declined by 18% year-on-year to Rs. 231.6 crore from Rs. 282.3 crore, while EBITDA margin contracted to 32% from 43.8%. Consolidated net profit declined by 30.5% to Rs. 118.8 crore compared with Rs. 171 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, net profit increased by 13.6% from Rs. 104.6 crore in the previous quarter.

items.t: Jim Cramer Calls Linde Plunge a Buying Opportunity, Highlights AI Spending Clarity
sum: Jim Cramer urged investors to buy shares of industrial gas giant Linde on Friday's dip, calling the company "one of the greatest stories of our time" during a volatile week for technology and industrial stocks.

Speaking on the CNBC Investing Club's "Morning Meeting," Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks recommended that new club members initiate a position in Linde (LIN) as shares fell nearly 6% despite a modest earnings beat. The decline came amid broader market crosscurrents, with bond yields surging to their highest levels since January 2025 and oil prices jumping after Iran said it attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
"This is an odd market," Cramer said, pointing to the 10-year Treasury yield's climb as the primary reason early morning stock gains evaporated.

Linde's electronics division delivered standout performance, posting 18% year-over-year growth and securing a major contract with Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM). However, investor sentiment soured over weakness in the company's home health care business. Management said it is evaluating strategic options for that unit, a proactive approach Marks praised.
"That's exactly what investors like to hear when a unit isn't generating the best results," Marks said.
Cramer's bullish call on Linde came against a backdrop of dramatic divergence in mega-cap technology earnings.

Amazon (AMZN) shares soared more than 14% following what the CNBC Investing Club characterized as a fantastic quarter. The cloud computing and e-commerce leader raised its capital expenditure guidance but eased investor concerns by detailing how it plans to monetize its artificial intelligence investments. Cramer urged investors to listen to CEO Andy Jassy's earnings call breakdown of the company's data center strategy.
